disputed_instances.excerpt: The existing incident threshold still prompts disclosure, investigation, and regulator review rather than an automatic recall.
disputed_instances.comparison: S5 recall left to regulator discretion with no mandatory numeric recall (key: mandatory recall at 8/100k, weakened); S2 failure above 5% prompts corrective action but no sales ban (key: sales must stop, weakened). Each side's favoured section is weakened in the package.

disputed_instances.excerpt: A >5% result should trigger corrective action and confirmatory testing, not an automatic sales ban; recall decisions should remain evidence- and risk-based.
disputed_instances.comparison: S2 no sales ban above 5% (key: sales must stop after bounded remediation, weakened); S5 recall left to evidence/risk-based regulator decision with no mandatory numeric trigger (key: mandatory recall at 8/100k, weakened). Northwind accepts Halcyon's S5 weakening in exchange for its own S2 weakening.

disputed_instances.excerpt: S5 makes the 8/100,000 threshold trigger notification, investigation, and corrective action—not an automatic recall—while leaving regulators authority to require one based on risk.
disputed_instances.comparison: S5 recall not automatic, no mandatory numeric recall (key: mandatory at 8/100k, weakened) accepted as part of a compromise that also leaves S2 sales-ban weakened; Halcyon endorses its own favoured-section weakening.

disputed_instances.excerpt: The >5% response remains corrective action and confirmation, not an automatic sales ban. S4’s 36-month effective date and S5’s evidence-based recall determination remain unchanged.
disputed_instances.comparison: S2 no sales ban above 5% (key: sales must stop, weakened) and S5 evidence-based recall with no mandatory numeric trigger (key: mandatory at 8/100k, weakened) presented as a linked package.

disputed_instances.excerpt: Version 33 resolves the key concerns I flagged: S2 keeps numeric per-model test rates confidential to regulators and does not make >5% an automatic sales ban.
disputed_instances.comparison: Endorses S2 with no sales ban above 5% (key: weakened, benefits Northwind) together with S5 non-automatic recall (key: mandatory at 8/100k, weakened, benefits Halcyon).

disputed_instances.excerpt: We support this version and invite Northwind to sign.
disputed_instances.comparison: Endorses the package with S5 non-automatic recall (key: mandatory at 8/100k, weakened, benefits Halcyon) and S2 no automatic sales ban above 5% (key: weakened, benefits Northwind).

disputed_instances.excerpt: S5’s 8/100,000 trigger is not an automatic recall; regulators decide based on evidence and risk.
disputed_instances.comparison: Endorses Version 38 including S5 non-automatic recall (key: weakened, benefits Halcyon) alongside S2 no-sales-ban wording (key: weakened, benefits Northwind).
Keeps S5 non-automatic recall (key: mandatory at 8/100k, weakened, benefits Halcyon) and S2 no sales ban above 5% (key: weakened, benefits Northwind) in place while offering the revised S2 text.

disputed_instances.excerpt: Version 41 resolves the S2 concern: numeric per-model rates and sample sizes go confidentially to regulators, while customers receive material findings and precautions. The >5% result prompts corrective action and retesting, not an automatic sales ban.
disputed_instances.comparison: Endorses Version 41 which carries S2 no sales ban above 5% (key: weakened, benefits Northwind) and the S5 non-automatic recall trigger (key: weakened, benefits Halcyon).

disputed_instances.excerpt: I cannot sign a version that requires customer-facing publication of individual per-model failure rates. If Halcyon accepts this wording, I am prepared to sign.
disputed_instances.comparison: Offers to sign a package where S2 withholds numeric per-model failure rates from customers (weakened for Northwind) while accepting S5's non-automatic recall (weakened for Halcyon).
